text:
This Place Delivery Agreement is dated 18 November 2026.

Parties

Party 1 — North East Mayoral Combined Authority (known as the North East Mayoral Strategic Authority) of The Lumen, St James’ Boulevard, Newcastle upon Tyne, NE4 5BZ (North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (MSA)).

Party 2 — Homes and Communities Agency (trading as Homes England) of 2nd floor, The Lumen, St James Boulevard, Newcastle Helix, Newcastle upon Tyne, NE4 5BZ (Homes England).

Party 3 — National Housing Bank Limited registered in England and Wales with company number 16862072 whose registered office is at Second Floor, The Lumen, Saint James’ Boulevard, Newcastle Upon Tyne, United Kingdom, NE4 5BZ (NHB or National Housing Bank).

Each a “Partner” and together the “Partners”.

Executive summary

This Place Delivery Agreement (PDA) represents a step change in how the North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (MSA), Homes England and the National Housing Bank will work together to deliver growth, housing and regeneration across the North East.

The North East has a clear ambition: to deliver more social and affordable homes, create stronger communities, unlock major regeneration opportunities and drive economic growth. Achieving that ambition requires more than alignment of priorities. It requires a delivery-focused partnership capable of moving at pace, aligning investment behind shared objectives, and providing the governance, capacity and expertise needed to translate ambition into visible change on the ground. Building on the foundations of the Strategic Place Partnership, this Agreement moves beyond a traditional place-based partnership model towards a shared delivery framework. It places delivery, investment and accountability at the heart of the relationship between the 3 organisations, creating a more integrated approach to identifying opportunities, resolving barriers, accelerating investment decisions and bringing forward development.

A central objective of the Agreement is to maximise housing delivery across all tenures while significantly increasing the supply of social and affordable homes. The North East continues to face substantial affordable housing pressures, and the Mayor has committed to increasing the delivery of social and affordable homes over the next decade. Through closer alignment of investment programmes, greater influence over funding decisions and a stronger regional pipeline of opportunities, this Agreement will help ensure that housing investment is targeted where it can have the greatest impact for communities.

The North East MSA and Homes England are already working together closely. The North East Major Projects Delivery Unit was formed in summer 2026, bringing together expertise across the 2 organisations. This Unit, the first of its kind nationally, is helping accelerate housing and regeneration delivery and strengthen the project pipeline.

This Place Delivery Agreement will build on this significant progress to date. It will strengthen the North East’s influence over housing and regeneration investment decisions by bringing decision-making closer to place. Through enhanced collaboration, the Mayor and North East MSA will play a stronger role in shaping investment priorities, ensuring that Homes England and National Housing Bank funding is aligned with regional ambitions, local needs and the objectives of the North East Growth Plan.

The partnership will focus delivery on a number of transformational priorities, including:

accelerating delivery of Mayoral Development Zones across Newcastle and Gateshead, Sunderland and Durham

supporting strategic infrastructure corridors, including the reinstatement of the Leamside Line, to unlock housing, employment and regeneration opportunities

building and maintaining a region-wide pipeline of investable housing and regeneration schemes

increasing the delivery of social and affordable housing and supporting council housebuilding ambitions

attracting institutional, public and private investment into the North East through a co-ordinated investment approach

unlocking complex and stalled sites through targeted intervention, development expertise and funding solutions

To support this ambition, the Agreement establishes a dedicated Housing Accelerator Team (HAT) as a Joint Delivery Unit between the North East MSA and Homes England, building on the foundations of the existing delivery unit which has been a trailblazer for joint working. The HAT will provide programme leadership, commercial expertise, technical capability and development capacity to accelerate delivery of strategic priorities, overcome barriers and support local authorities, registered providers and development partners.

Importantly, this Agreement is not solely focused on projects. By strengthening regional capability, creating clearer routes to investment and embedding a culture of delivery, the partnership will ensure the region has the skills, expertise and institutional capacity required to deliver ambitious housing and regeneration programmes over the coming decades.

The Agreement also introduces significantly enhanced governance and accountability arrangements. A shared performance framework, direct oversight from the Mayor, a Strategic Housing Board involving senior leaders from all 3 organisations (North East MSA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank) and dedicated executive leadership arrangements will ensure a clear focus on outcomes, delivery performance and problem-solving.

At its core, this Agreement reflects the principles of devolution and the government’s commitment to rewiring the state. It recognises that sustainable growth is best achieved when local leadership is matched by national investment and delivery capability. By bringing together the Mayor’s strategic leadership, Homes England’s expertise and the National Housing Bank’s investment capacity, the North East will be better placed to secure investment, unlock opportunity and deliver lasting benefits for communities.

Above all, it is an agreement focused on outcomes. It is about delivering homes faster, unlocking strategic sites sooner, investing more effectively and ensuring that growth translates into tangible improvements in the lives of people and communities across the North East. Through this Agreement, the partners commit to working together with pace, purpose and shared accountability to deliver the ambitions of the North East Growth Plan and create lasting economic and social impact for future generations.

Key priorities for this PDA

Delivering the North East’s most significant growth and regeneration opportunities

Accelerating Mayoral Development Zones (MDZs) — focusing investment, resources and delivery capacity on transformational regeneration opportunities that can unlock homes, jobs, infrastructure and sustainable economic growth, including:

supporting delivery of the Newcastle and Gateshead MDZ Strategic Regeneration Framework, unlocking around 16,000 new homes and providing a long-term programme for regeneration and investment over the next 25 years

accelerating delivery of the Sunderland MDZ, supporting Sunderland Riverside and unlocking homes, jobs and commercial development opportunities

bringing forward the Durham MDZ to support new homes, commercial growth and city centre regeneration

Supporting the reinstatement of the Leamside Line as a major growth and investment corridor — improving connectivity between communities, employment sites and key economic assets while unlocking the potential for around 22,000 new homes. Reopening the line would stimulate investment, support regeneration and create new opportunities for sustainable growth along one of the North East’s most significant development corridors.

Building and maintaining a strong regional pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities across the North East — ensuring investment supports both major urban regeneration programmes and locally led growth priorities in communities across the region. Ensuring that a robust pipeline is in place will form the basis of the shared commitment to accelerating the pace of housing delivery across the region.

Putting housing investment decisions closer to place

Empowering the North East MSA to shape housing investment and delivery priorities across all typologies and tenures — ensuring decisions reflect local housing needs, growth ambitions and regeneration opportunities.

Giving the Mayor a stronger role in shaping social and affordable housing investment — through regionally delegated Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP) Continuous Market Engagement (CME) arrangements, providing greater influence over where funding is targeted to maximise delivery.

Aligning Homes England and National Housing Bank investment with the North East Growth Plan, Housing Strategy and wider regeneration priorities — creating a more co-ordinated approach to housing delivery, infrastructure investment and economic growth.

Giving the region a stronger voice in how national housing funding is deployed — helping to unlock stalled sites, accelerate delivery and maximise the impact of public investment across the North East.

Accelerating social and affordable housing and council house delivery

Ensuring the delivery of the Mayoral ambition to increase social and affordable housing delivery between 2026 to 2036 — addressing the shortage of 2,600 affordable homes per year.

Maximising the impact of the North East’s £1.1 billion SAHP indicative spend amount.

Supporting local authorities, registered providers and delivery partners to enhance, prioritise and deliver the existing North East Housing Pipeline.

Unlocking investment at scale

Establishing a connected investment ecosystem for housing and regeneration, bringing together public investment, development expertise and private capital — including through a regional Good Growth Fund—to improve viability, unlock complex sites and accelerate delivery across the North East.

Developing a portfolio of investable housing and regeneration opportunities, capable of attracting National Housing Bank, institutional and private sector investment into the region.

Building long-term delivery capacity

Establishing the Housing Accelerator Team (HAT) as a Joint Delivery Unit between the North East MSA and Homes England — providing the programme leadership, technical expertise and investment capacity needed to turn regional priorities into investable projects, overcome barriers and accelerate housing, regeneration and economic growth.

Strengthening local capability and delivery capacity across the region — supporting local authorities, registered providers and partners to bring forward increasingly complex housing and regeneration schemes.

Creating a long-term delivery platform for the North East — ensuring the region has the expertise, partnerships and institutional capacity required to deliver ambitious growth and regeneration programmes over the coming decades.

Aligning housing delivery with wider economic growth, employment and productivity ambitions — ensuring that investment in housing supports stronger communities, attracts investment and contributes to long-term regional prosperity.

Strengthening accountability and governance

The formation of this Agreement will create significantly enhanced accountability through a shared performance framework and direct reporting arrangements to the Mayor.

This Agreement represents an enhanced model of place-based delivery. By combining local leadership, devolved influence, dedicated delivery capability, aligned investment and stronger accountability, the North East MSA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank will work together to deliver more homes, unlock regeneration, attract investment and drive long-term economic growth across the North East.

Commencement and term

This Agreement shall commence on the date hereof and shall continue for an initial period of 3 years (subject to an annual review) and shall thereafter continue for such further period or periods as shall be agreed in writing between the parties, provided always that any party may give not less than 90 days prior written notice to the others to terminate this PDA at any time.

1. Strategic context: The North East growth ambitions

The North East is a region with internationally recognised strengths in advanced manufacturing, clean energy, offshore industries, life sciences, digital technologies and innovation. These sectors are supported by globally significant assets, including world-class universities, strategic ports, major employment sites, innovation districts and nationally important energy infrastructure.

The North East Mayoral Strategic Authority

1.1 The North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (MSA) is led by a directly elected mayor and cabinet and serves a population of more than 2 million people across 7 local authority areas:

County Durham

Gateshead

Newcastle

North Tyneside

Northumberland

South Tyneside

Sunderland

1.2 Together, these areas form a highly connected economic, housing and labour market, encompassing major urban centres, thriving towns, extensive rural landscapes and over 100 miles of coastline. This diversity gives the North East a distinctive economic geography and a unique combination of growth opportunities.

Growth Ambitions and Opportunities

1.3 The North East Local Growth Plan 2025 to 2035 (the Local Growth Plan) sets out a long-term vision for a stronger, more productive and more inclusive regional economy. At its heart, the Local Growth Plan is built around 5 missions:

1 — Home to a growing and vibrant economy for all.

2 — Home of the green energy revolution.

3 — A welcoming home to global trade.

4 — Home of real opportunity.

5 — A North East we are proud to call home.

1.4 Through investment, regeneration and strong partnerships, the Local Growth Plan aims to unlock sustainable economic growth, create better jobs, accelerate housing delivery, attract private sector investment and ensure that the benefits of prosperity are shared by communities across the region. It provides a clear framework for transforming places, improving opportunities for residents and strengthening the North East’s competitiveness as a great place to live, work, invest and do business.

1.5 In July 2026, the Mayor launched the Plan for Homes, setting out a bold ambition to accelerate housebuilding across the North East and ensure that more people can access good-quality, affordable homes. The Plan for Homes focuses on unlocking stalled and complex regeneration sites, accelerating brownfield development, attracting investment, increasing the delivery of social and affordable housing, and working in partnership to remove barriers to development.

1.6 The Plan for Homes brings together investment from the Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP) and the North East MSA’s £143 million Housing Delivery Fund, creating a co-ordinated approach to housing and regeneration. Together, these programmes will support the delivery of 15,000 social and affordable homes over the coming years, while also unlocking wider economic growth and regeneration opportunities across the region. The Plan is built around 3 strategic objectives:

improving housing quality, affordability and inclusion

delivering more good-quality homes and unlocking investment

creating sustainable places and supporting economic growth

Housing and regeneration in the North East

1.7 Delivering the ambitions set out in the North East Local Growth Plan and the Mayor’s Plan for Homes requires a co-ordinated approach to housing, regeneration, infrastructure and economic development. The availability of good-quality homes and attractive, well-connected places is critical to supporting economic growth, attracting and retaining talent, enabling investment and ensuring communities can benefit from new opportunities.

1.8 While the North East offers a diverse range of places and communities, many areas continue to face longstanding economic, physical and housing market challenges. Addressing disparities in housing quality, increasing housing supply across all tenures and bringing forward regeneration opportunities will be essential to creating sustainable and inclusive growth.

1.9 The region faces a number of significant barriers to delivery. These include development viability, fragmented land ownership, site remediation requirements, infrastructure costs, housing need and capacity constraints across the public and private sectors. Many of the North East’s most important growth and regeneration opportunities are located on complex brownfield sites that require co-ordinated intervention and investment before development can take place.

Key challenges include:

development viability and access to gap funding

brownfield land assembly, remediation and site readiness

rising homelessness and increasing housing need

delivering more social, affordable and council homes

infrastructure and enabling investment requirements

local authority and delivery partner capacity

market conditions and investor confidence

the long delivery timescales associated with major regeneration projects

1.10 Development viability remains the most significant constraint on housing and regeneration delivery across the North East. Construction, infrastructure and supply chain costs have increased substantially, while development values across much of the region remain comparatively low. This challenge is particularly acute on brownfield and regeneration sites, where abnormal costs associated with remediation, land assembly and infrastructure can make development unviable without public sector support.

1.11 The challenge facing the North East is not a lack of ambition, opportunity or development capacity. The region has a strong pipeline of housing and regeneration projects capable of supporting economic growth, transforming communities and delivering new homes at scale. However, many of these opportunities require significant intervention and investment to overcome viability barriers and unlock delivery. Securing the tools, funding and flexibility needed to address these challenges will be critical to accelerating housing delivery, attracting private investment and realising the region’s long-term growth ambitions.

Strategic opportunities

1.12 The North East MSA has an ambitious programme of housing-led regeneration and place-based investment opportunities capable of transforming communities, supporting economic growth, improving productivity and accelerating housing delivery.

1.13 Through its North East Growth Plan and the Mayoral Development Zones, the North East MSA is seeking to establish the North East as a national exemplar for housing delivery and regeneration, working in partnership with Homes England, the National Housing Bank and other key delivery partners.

1.14 Key opportunities include the 3 Mayoral Development Zones; Newcastle and Gateshead, Sunderland and Durham. The Leamside Line and the existing North East Housing Pipeline across the 7 local authority areas are also opportunities. Collectively these opportunities provide the basis for a long-term pipeline of investment capable of delivering new homes, commercial growth, improved connectivity and enhanced quality of place.

1.15 A pipeline of strategic place-based acquisitions is currently in development. These represent timely opportunities to acquire land in MDZ areas which will form the basis of future strategic residential-led pipeline. At present, the proposal is for acquisitions to be owned and managed by Homes England on behalf of the North East MSA, subject to any required separate legal agreements, governance approvals and funding arrangements.

1.16 The strategic place-based acquisitions will also encompass work exploring the potential of innovative land interventions, including the potential for a pilot proposition evergreen fund and securing mayoral support for reform of current land classification arrangements.

2. Going further, faster and rewiring the state

2.1 The North East Strategic Place Partnership (SPP) is a long-term partnership between the North East MSA and Homes England to accelerate housing delivery, regeneration and economic growth. The partnership brings together investment, expertise and delivery capacity to unlock strategic housing and regeneration opportunities across the region, particularly on complex brownfield sites where market barriers constrain delivery. Through a shared pipeline of projects and co-ordinated investment approach, the SPP provides a mechanism to align local priorities with national funding and support the delivery of housing-led growth, thriving communities and sustainable places across the North East.

Since its establishment, the SPP has helped unlock:

more than £220 million of investment in support of the Mayor’s housing and regeneration priorities

2,043 affordable homes

capacity to deliver over 3,400 homes

2.2 All partners now recognise we need to go much further, much faster, and show how we are rewiring the state to better serve the North East. The PDA represents the next evolution of the SPP, moving beyond collaboration towards co-delivery.

2.3 Together, the partners will establish a new model of place-based delivery capable of accelerating housing delivery, unlocking regeneration opportunities and supporting sustainable economic growth across the North East. The new joint Housing Accelerator Team (HAT), operating under the strategic leadership of the North East Mayor and North East MSA, will provide a delivery framework through which strategic ambition can be translated into investable propositions, faster decision-making and tangible delivery outcomes.

Place Delivery Agreement: a new strategic framework to serve places and local leaders

2.4 This PDA establishes a framework through which North East MSA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank will align resources, expertise, capacity, investment and delivery activity to accelerate housing delivery, unlock regeneration opportunities and support the growth ambitions of the North East.

2.5 The Agreement focuses on a number of shared strategic priorities where a co-ordinated approach can have the greatest impact in unlocking delivery, overcoming barriers, attracting investment and accelerating transformational housing and regeneration outcomes. These priorities reflect the shared ambition of all 3 organisations to use housing, regeneration and place-based investment as drivers of economic growth, productivity and inclusive prosperity.

2.6 Alongside these strategic priorities, partners will continue to develop and maintain the North East Housing Pipeline, providing a shared evidence base to inform the targeting of resources, specialist support, investment and intervention across the region. This co-ordinated approach will help ensure that opportunities are identified early, delivery challenges are addressed collectively and investment is directed where it can have the greatest impact.

2.7 The priorities set out below will form the initial focus of activity under this PDA. They will be reviewed periodically by the partners to ensure resources remain focused on the opportunities where joint intervention can deliver the greatest strategic impact.

2.8 Fundamentally, this framework is intended to ensure that local priorities, national capability and long-term investment are aligned around a common set of delivery objectives.

3. Theme A: Delivering large-scale transformation projects

3.1 A core purpose of this PDA is to provide the Mayor and local leaders across the North East with the tools they need to deliver their most ambitious housing, regeneration and growth priorities. This PDA recognises that achieving transformational change requires more than aligned ambition; it requires dedicated delivery capability, co-ordinated investment and long-term partnership.

3.2 Through the HAT, Homes England and the National Housing Bank will support the North East MSA to deliver a prioritised portfolio of major strategic projects. Bringing together land, funding, specialist technical expertise and investment capability and powers, the HAT will help accelerate delivery, unlock complex opportunities and support the delivery of places that make the greatest contribution to economic growth and housing supply.

3.3 The strategic projects identified below will form the initial focus of this PDA and represent opportunities where joint intervention can have the greatest impact on delivery outcomes across the North East.

Strategic place priority 1: Mayoral Development Zones

3.4 The Newcastle and Gateshead Mayoral Development Zone represents a once-in-a-generation regeneration opportunity, with capacity for more than 16,000 new homes, over 3 million square feet of commercial and employment space and billions of pounds of potential investment. Major opportunities at the Eastern and Western Urban Villages including Forth Yards, Gateshead Town Centre, Newcastle City Core, St James’ Quarter and the Innovation Quarter will create new neighbourhoods, support business growth, strengthen the visitor economy and establish the Urban Core as a leading destination for living, innovation, culture and investment.

3.5 Together, these projects have the potential to at least double the resident population, attract private sector investment at scale and drive long-term economic growth across Newcastle, Gateshead and the wider North East.

3.6 The scale, complexity and strategic importance of the opportunity requires a co-ordinated approach across land assembly, infrastructure provision, planning, investment and delivery. Homes England will work with the North East MSA, Newcastle City Council and Gateshead Council to support the delivery of a complex pipeline of housing, regeneration and infrastructure projects, bringing together investment, expertise and delivery capacity to unlock sites, overcome barriers and accelerate long-term growth. This collaborative approach will help create a co-ordinated regeneration programme capable of delivering homes, jobs and investment at scale over the coming decades.

3.7 Sunderland Mayoral Development Zone — Sunderland Riverside represents one of the North East’s most successful regeneration stories and a nationally recognised example of long-term place-based transformation. Significant investment over recent years has helped reconnect the city delivering major employment sites, new commercial development, high-quality public realm, cultural destinations and transformational infrastructure. Building on this strong foundation, Sunderland Riverside continues to offer substantial opportunities for housing, employment and mixed-use development, creating new neighbourhoods and supporting the city’s continued economic growth.

3.8 Together with wider regeneration initiatives across Sunderland, the programme will attract further private sector investment, strengthen the city centre, create new homes and jobs, and reinforce Sunderland’s position as one of the UK’s leading cities for innovation, advanced manufacturing and clean energy.

3.9 Durham Mayoral Development Zone is driving forward plans for Aykley Heads in the Durham Innovation District, through a strategic partnership between Durham County Council, its joint venture delivery partner Muse, Durham University and the North East MSA. Aykley Heads is expected to deliver around 400,000 square feet of high-quality workspace across 4 phases. While the primary focus of the project is on delivering commercial space, there is likely to be a residential component as part of the vision of a mixed-use innovation district.

Strategic place priority 2: Leamside Line

3.10 The reinstatement of the Leamside Line represents one of the North East’s most significant opportunities to align transport investment with housing delivery, regeneration and economic growth. Reopening the route would create a strategic growth corridor connecting communities, employment locations and key economic assets across the region, while unlocking the potential for around 22,000 new homes and supporting major regeneration opportunities along the corridor.

3.11 Realising the full benefits of the Leamside Line will require a co-ordinated approach to transport planning, land assembly, infrastructure investment, housing delivery and regeneration. Aligning investment and development activity around the corridor will be critical to maximising the wider economic, social and place-based benefits generated by the scheme.

3.12 Partners will work together to develop a coherent and investable long-term proposition that brings together transport, housing, regeneration and infrastructure interventions into a single programme. This integrated approach will help unlock strategic sites, attract private sector investment, accelerate housing delivery and support the creation of well-connected, sustainable communities along one of the region’s most important growth corridors.

Theme B: Housing and Regeneration Pipeline

3.13 Alongside the flagship regeneration opportunities identified above, Homes England and North East MSA will maintain and enhance the existing North East Housing Pipeline.

3.14 The pipeline includes opportunities requiring different forms of support, including:

investment-ready opportunities that are deliverable in the near-term

projects where co-development or the targeted application of expertise or enabling investment will unlock delivery

strategic growth and regeneration opportunities where a more integrated approach is required to unlock transformational change

3.15 Through this PDA, all partner organisations will work together to identify where aligned investment, expertise, delivery support and market engagement can have the greatest impact in unlocking homes, growth and regeneration outcomes across the region.

3.16 Early work will include:

a) Ensuring the delivery of the Mayor’s ambition to provide around 15,000 new social and affordable homes across the North East between 2026 and 2036, using all available routes including the Strategic Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP), Section 106 agreements, Homes England funding, and complementary investment and finance products through the National Housing Bank and other partners. Working collaboratively to unlock stalled sites, accelerate delivery, and maximise opportunities to increase the supply of affordable housing across the region.

b) Maximising the impact of the North East’s £1.1 billion SAHP indicative spend amount to deliver thousands of social and affordable homes and council homes.

c) Completing the call for sites to inform the allocation of the North East MSA’s National Housing Delivery Fund (NHDF) component of the Integrated Settlement — this has involved collaborative working to review submissions, consider viability, deliverability and value for money, and make recommendations on the prioritisation and phasing of investment.

3.17 The HAT will also support delivery of schemes on Homes England owned sites, including the large 875 home Cottingwood urban extension to Morpeth, the 310 home Annitsford Farm in North Tyneside, and Lower Ouseburn in Newcastle.

3.18 Building on work already underway we will also implement a new approach to unlock the true social value of public sector land via this PDA. This could test a more co-ordinated approach to identifying, assembling and unlocking public land opportunities across the North East. Through the HAT, working with wider public sector partners, the partners will identify a portfolio of priority sites, explore barriers to delivery, and assess the potential for a longer-term public sector land programme that could accelerate housing delivery, regeneration and economic growth rather than just recycle receipts.

4. Theme C: Shared thematic priorities

4.1 The partners recognise that achieving the scale of change envisaged through the Local Growth Plan requires more than investment alone. It requires greater alignment between local priorities, national capability and investment decision-making. Through this Agreement, Homes England and the National Housing Bank will support the North East MSA to create a more integrated and locally responsive system, ensuring that the full range of housing, regeneration and growth interventions are aligned behind the Mayor’s priorities.

4.2 This PDA represents an opportunity to bring decision-making, delivery capability and investment closer to place. This PDA will strengthen the North East’s influence over key elements of the housing and regeneration system, enabling local priorities to shape the deployment of funding, specialist expertise and delivery support.

4.3 The thematic priorities set out below focus on those areas where greater local influence, co-ordinated action and aligned investment can have the greatest impact on housing delivery, regeneration outcomes and economic growth. Together, they will help create the conditions required to unlock a stronger pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities and support the delivery of the North East’s long-term ambitions.

Social and affordable housing and council housebuilding

4.4 Affordable housing is one of the clearest examples of how this PDA will bring decision-making, delivery capability and accountability closer to place.

4.5 Through this Agreement, the HAT will ensure affordable housing investment is aligned with the Mayor’s priorities for growth, regeneration and housing delivery. By combining regional decision-making with dedicated delivery capability and specialist affordable housing expertise, the partnership will enable investment decisions to be shaped more directly by local priorities and delivery opportunities.

4.6 The North East has an indicative spend amount of £1.1 billion through the SAHP, creating a significant opportunity to accelerate social and affordable housing and council house delivery across the region. Through the HAT, partners will work together to maximise the impact of this investment, increase the pace and scale of delivery, and ensure affordable housing investment supports wider regeneration, economic growth and placemaking ambitions.

4.7 Through this partnership, the partners will seek to facilitate the delivery of the Mayor’s ambition to increase social and affordable housing delivery between 2026-2036, addressing the shortage of 2,600 affordable homes per year alongside broader regeneration and economic growth outcomes.

4.8 This focus on delivery will reflect the North East MSA and government’s increased emphasis on social and council housing and will seek to explore innovative delivery models such as Registered Providers building homes on behalf of councils.

4.9 The partners will maintain and enhance the North East Housing Pipeline, ensuring activity and investment are directed towards opportunities that can unlock or accelerate delivery, address housing need and contribute to the ambitions of the North East Local Growth Plan. This will include:

SAHP decisions on Continuous Market Engagement (CME) will be delegated by Homes England to the Regional SAHP team (within agreed thresholds) with the HAT providing the governance forum to enable investment decisions to be locally led and determined

the Mayor and North East MSA being given full visibility of the affordable housing pipeline data in their area — through the HAT and enhanced governance, they will be included in the affordable housing pipeline review and CME assessment process providing local insights and data to develop proposals

the Mayor and North East MSA being involved in the assessment and decision-making process for further procurement rounds or extensions to existing Strategic Partnership allocations that affect the region

SAHP CME investment decisions being made, via this PDA, the HAT or respective governance structures for a definitive decision through monthly governance

working with Registered Provider Strategic Partners operating within the SAHP to align investment plans and develop a co-ordinated pipeline of social and affordable housing opportunities across the region, supporting delivery of the Mayor’s affordable housing and regeneration priorities

4.10 Recognising the government’s ambition to significantly increase council house delivery, Homes England will support the North East MSA to:

review the barriers to delivery of council housing and work collaboratively with local authorities to implement the preferred approaches including the potential to align with other thematic areas including land, industrialised construction and other forms of investment

bring empty homes back into use and other improvements to existing stock including where there are positive links to be made to other policy areas such as reduced use of temporary accommodation

Place-based investment and finance

4.11 The delivery of the North East MSA housing and regeneration ambitions will require investment at a scale that cannot be achieved through grant funding alone. Unlocking transformational opportunities across the region will depend on the ability to combine public and private capital, recycle investment over time and develop investable propositions capable of attracting long-term institutional funding.

4.12 The National Housing Bank, launched by Homes England in 2026, has been established to accelerate the delivery of new homes and mixed-use regeneration schemes through flexible public investment. Backed by up to £16 billion of debt, equity and guarantee products, the bank is designed to work with national, regional and local partners to unlock housing delivery, crowd-in private capital and support the government’s ambition to deliver 1.5 million homes while delivering a positive financial return for the Exchequer.

4.13 The North East MSA and Homes England share an ambition to use this PDA as a platform to develop innovative approaches to place-based investment, enhancing the existing North East Housing Pipeline of investable housing and regeneration opportunities and increasing the scale of private capital investment into the North East.

4.14 As part of this Agreement, the National Housing Bank will actively seek opportunities to amplify the region’s local investment fund supporting housing and regeneration ambition and the Mayor’s priorities to attract wider investment using its lending, equity or guarantee capacity.

4.15 The National Housing Bank will support the development of a portfolio of investment opportunities capable of unlocking a significantly greater level of private and institutional capital investment over time, including from the National Housing Bank.

4.16 Partners will work together to identify and develop housing-led regeneration, infrastructure-enabled growth, mixed-use development and strategic land opportunities that have the potential to unlock significantly greater levels of private and institutional investment over time.

4.17 The partnership will seek to:

maintain and enhance the prioritised pipeline of investable housing and regeneration opportunities across the North East

align National Housing Bank products and investment capabilities with mayoral growth and regeneration priorities

maximise the deployment of National Housing Bank products in the North East through targeted promotion, advice and support to the sector

crowd-in institutional and private-sector capital alongside public investment

explore innovative approaches to land, infrastructure and development finance that accelerate delivery and improve viability

establish the North East as a national exemplar for place-based investment and housing-led economic growth

develop replicable investment models that can be applied across a wider pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities

4.18 The North East MSA allocation of the National Housing Delivery Fund will operate alongside National Housing Bank investment activity, helping to address barriers to delivery and develop the investable pipeline required to attract future bank support. Together, these funding streams have the potential to create a flexible source of capital to unlock strategic housing and regeneration priorities across the region.

4.19 By combining devolved funding, National Housing Bank investment and private capital, the North East will test a new model of place-based investment designed to accelerate delivery, improve viability and support long-term economic growth.

Skills and capacity for housing growth ambitions

4.20 Delivering the scale of housing and regeneration envisaged by the Local Growth Plan will require sufficient development capacity, technical expertise and workforce skills across both the public and private sectors. Addressing these challenges is critical to accelerating housing delivery, supporting economic growth and ensuring the North East can maximise the opportunities presented by major regeneration and infrastructure investment.

4.21 Homes England and the North East MSA share an ambition to position the North East as a region of excellence for housing delivery, placemaking and innovation in construction. The partners will work collaboratively to ensure the North East region has the workforce skills, development capacity and technical expertise required to support housing growth ambitions and wider economic development priorities. Addressing these challenges is critical to accelerating housing delivery, supporting economic growth and ensuring the region can maximise the opportunities presented by major regeneration and infrastructure investment.

4.22 The partners will support the development of construction skills pipelines, promote apprenticeships and employment opportunities.

4.23 The partners will seek to:

align housing investment with local skills, employment and economic growth strategies

support delivery of the North East Local Growth Plan by strengthening the construction workforce, increasing productivity through modern methods of construction and supporting the delivery of new homes across the region

identify and address skills shortages within key housing and infrastructure occupations that may impact delivery of strategic housing sites, with activity informed by the North East Local Skills Improvement Plan, ensuring that investment responds to employer-led workforce requirements across construction and related sectors

align housing investment with the ambitions of the New Deal for North East Workers, using housing and regeneration programmes to support employment, apprenticeships and workforce development

align housing delivery with skills, employment and economic development programmes to maximise local economic benefits and create pathways into high-quality jobs, including adopting recommendations from Alan Milburn’s young people and work review

support the development of a skilled construction workforce to deliver the region’s growth ambitions through collaboration with local authorities, employers, training providers, further and higher education institutions, and industry partners

promote careers in construction and the built environment, with a particular focus on attracting young people, women and underrepresented groups into the sector

explore opportunities to utilise Homes England programmes and investments to stimulate local supply chains and create high-quality employment opportunities for North East residents

4.24 Through this PDA, Homes England will support the North East MSA to ensure that the skills, capacity and innovation required to support long-term housing and regeneration growth are embedded across the region, strengthening the foundations for sustainable delivery and creating a model that can be replicated nationally.

5. Next steps: Delivery, governance and implementation

5.1 A Joint Strategic Housing Board will be formed involving the Mayor, the Chairs of Homes England and the National Housing Bank, and the Chief Executives of all 3 partners, providing direct oversight of investment priorities, delivery performance and funding alignment across the North East’s housing pipeline.

5.2 To allow for quicker decision-making the day-to-day Homes England and National Housing Bank responsibility for delivery of this PDA will be delegated to the Homes England executive director for the North East.

5.3 There will be the introduction of quarterly senior sponsor meetings to oversee delivery, resolve barriers and hold the partnership to account for agreed outcomes and a twice-yearly senior leaders meeting to review PDA progress, delivery performance and shared priorities.

5.4 North East MSA’s Assistant Director of Place and a nominated Homes England director will lead the HAT. The HAT operates in an advisory and co-ordinating capacity only and shall not have delegated authority to bind any partner or make decisions on behalf of any partner unless expressly authorised under that partner’s own governance arrangements.

5.5 This new single framework will help to strengthen local capability to support delivery, while recognising a desire to go further in boosting the capacity, expertise and sharing of good practice across the public and private sector partners in the sub-region via a focused programme of activity. The Delivery Plan is a management document and shall not create legally binding obligations or financial commitments.

5.6 The HAT will provide greater visibility and accountability to the Mayor, giving the Mayor the control, influence and resources needed to build the homes and places communities require and to hold partners to account for delivery.

5.7 North East MSA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank commit to progressing a joint Delivery Plan outlining key tasks, milestones and resourcing commitments underpinned by a governance framework which delivers on the principles outlined in this PDA.

Partnership commitments

5.8 The partners commit to:

align resources around mayoral priorities

maintain and enhance the North East’s shared strategic development and investment pipeline

jointly identify and resolve barriers

co-ordinate stakeholder engagement through the North East Developer Network

share intelligence and investment planning

support delivery through a dedicated HAT

5.9 This PDA will operate on a 3-year basis and will be reviewed annually to ensure it remains aligned with evolving national policy, mayoral priorities, market conditions and delivery opportunities. This PDA is intended to provide a single framework while retaining sufficient flexibility to respond to changing circumstances and emerging priorities.

Delivery of the PDA will be supported through:

a rolling delivery programme maintained through the HAT responding to mayoral priorities, interventions and opportunities requiring joint action

a detailed annual Delivery Plan, agreed following approval of this PDA, translating strategic priorities into specific actions, responsibilities, milestones and resource commitments

an annual review process to refresh delivery priorities, resource allocations and pipeline activity without requiring the full PDA to be renegotiated

regular monitoring and performance reporting through the governance and accountability arrangements within this PDA, enabling partners to track progress, identify emerging risks and agree corrective action where required

5.10 The partners acknowledge that successful delivery will require ongoing collaboration between Homes England, the National Housing Bank, North East MSA and wider delivery partners, including local authorities, government departments, infrastructure providers, registered providers, investors and other stakeholders.

North East Housing Accelerator Team

5.11 The Housing Accelerator Team (HAT) will provide a single delivery interface between North East MSA and Homes England and drive implementation of agreed priorities through the following functions:

programme management

opportunity identification

pipeline development

major housing project delivery

investment co-ordination

risk management

performance monitoring

Governance and accountability

5.18 The Governance Framework will be developed further through the Delivery Plan and will include:

creating significantly enhanced accountability through a shared performance framework and direct reporting arrangements to the Mayor

establishing strengthened oversight arrangements involving the Mayor, the Chairs of Homes England and the National Housing Bank and the Chief Executives of all 3 organisations

introducing quarterly senior sponsor meetings to oversee delivery, resolve barriers and hold the partnership to account for agreed outcomes

5.19 In recognition of the commitment to create an even more responsive and re-wired delivery body as outlined in the Housing Minister’s letter and to bring decision-making and accountability closer to impacted communities, the parties will commit in parallel to review existing delegations, reporting and accountability frameworks.

5.20 Communications and stakeholder engagement activity will similarly be reviewed to maximise Homes England impact. Homes England will ensure information on planned activity within the geographical area of the North East will be shared with North East MSA in advance via the HAT.

Delivery plan

5.21 This PDA will be supported by a detailed Delivery Plan which will provide the primary mechanism for co-ordinating delivery activity and monitoring progress against agreed commitments.

5.22 The Delivery Plan will:

translate the strategic priorities and commitments set out within this PDA into deliverable programmes, projects and interventions

set out key milestones, outputs, funding requirements, resource commitments and critical dependencies, identify risks, constraints and barriers to delivery, together with proposed mitigation measures and required decisions

establish performance measures, success indicators and reporting arrangements

maintain a forward pipeline of opportunities and activities to support delivery of shared priorities

identify areas where additional collaboration, investment or intervention may be required to achieve agreed outcomes

5.23 Each partnership commitment included within the Delivery Plan will identify:

the agreed commitment or activity

the responsible organisation or organisations

a named lead owner

target completion or review dates

expected outputs and outcomes

success measures and monitoring arrangements

5.24 Following completion of this PDA, the HAT will co-ordinate preparation of the Delivery Plan and maintain it as a live document throughout the life of this PDA.

The partners will agree:

the timetable for the preparation and implementation of the Delivery Plan

the lead organisation responsible for co-ordinating drafting and updates

governance arrangements for review, endorsement and approval

the senior officers authorised to approve revisions and updates

reporting arrangements to support effective oversight and accountability

Annual review

5.25 This PDA will be subject to an annual review led by the HAT and overseen through the governance arrangements referred to in this PDA. It will report to the Mayor and the Chief Executive and Chair of Homes England.

5.26 The review will:

assess progress against the commitments and success measures set out in the Delivery Plan

consider emerging opportunities, risks and policy developments

review resource requirements and delivery capacity

refresh the rolling programme of activity and priority projects

recommend amendments to the Delivery Plan where required

5.27 Unless otherwise agreed by the partners, changes arising through the annual review process will be managed through updates to the Delivery Plan and will not require this PDA itself to be redrafted or re-executed.

5.28 This approach will ensure that this PDA remains a stable long-term framework while enabling partners to adapt delivery activity in response to changing circumstances and opportunities.

6. General

6.1 The schedule to this PDA is incorporated into and forms part of this PDA.

6.2 This PDA shall not create a relationship of partnership joint venture and or, agent relationships between the partners, nor authorise the partners to make or enter into any commitments for or on behalf of another partner.

6.3 The partners acknowledge and agree that decisions regarding investment, financial and other commitments shall be subject to each partner’s governance procedures and requirements and this PDA shall not bind any of the partners in this respect.

6.4 Nothing contained or implied in this PDA or any consent or approval granted pursuant to this PDA shall prejudice, fetter, restrict or affect the rights, powers, duties and obligations of the parties in the exercise of their respective statutory functions and such rights, powers, duties and obligations may be as fully and effectually exercised as if the relevant partner was not a party to this PDA. Each partner shall remain solely responsible for its own decisions and compliance with applicable legal, financial, procurement, subsidy control and governance requirements and any approval, consent, direction or authority given by the relevant partner as local or statutory authority (as the case may be) shall not be or be deemed to be an approval, consent, direction or authority given under this PDA and vice versa.

6.5 References to the Mayor, Cabinet or North East MSA within this Agreement are descriptive only and shall not replace or supersede the North East MSA’s constitutional decision-making requirements, scheme of delegation or statutory governance procedures.

6.6 No partner shall issue a public announcement, media statement or publicity material referring to this Agreement without prior consultation with the other affected partners, except where disclosure is required by law.

Schedule

1. Confidentiality

1.1 In this clause the following words and expressions have the following meaning:

Confidential Information means the terms of this PDA and all information whether oral or written (on whatever medium stored) relating to this PDA disclosed or made available, directly or indirectly by one party or its employees, officers, representatives or advisers to the other party or its employees, officers, representatives or advisers but excludes any information which:

(i) at the time of such disclosure is, or subsequently becomes, publicly available;

(ii) at the time of such disclosure is, or subsequently becomes, available to the Recipient from a person who, to the Recipient’s knowledge, is not under any confidential obligation in respect of that information; or

(iii) has been independently acquired by a Party without breaching any of their respective obligations in this PDA.

1.2 Each Party recognises that under this PDA it may receive Confidential Information belonging to the other.

1.3 Each Party agrees to treat all Confidential Information belonging to the other as confidential and not to disclose such Confidential Information or any other confidential information relating to each other arising or coming to its attention in the course of this PDA to any third party without the prior written consent of the other Party and agrees not to use such Confidential Information for any purpose other than that for which it is supplied under this PDA.

1.4 The obligations of confidence referred to in Clause 1.3 shall not apply to any Confidential Information which:

(a) is in, or which comes into, the public domain otherwise than by reason of a breach of this PDA or of any other duty of confidentiality relating to that information; or

(b) is obtained from a third party without that third party being under an obligation (express or implied) to keep the information confidential; or

(c) is lawfully in the possession of the other Party before the date of this PDA and in respect of which that Party is not under an existing obligation of confidentiality; or

(d) is independently developed without access to the Confidential Information of the other Party.

1.5 Each Party will be permitted to disclose Confidential Information to the extent that it is required to do so:

(a) to enable the disclosing party to perform its obligations under this PDA; or

(b) by any applicable law or by a court, arbitral or administrative tribunal in the course of proceedings before it including without limitation any requirement for disclosure under Freedom of Information Laws (as defined in clause 2) and the Parties acknowledge that any lists or schedules provided by it outlining Confidential Information are of indicative value only and that the other party may nevertheless be obliged to disclose such confidential information; or

(c) by any regulatory body (including any investment exchange) acting in the course of proceedings before it or acting in the course of its duties; or

(d) in order to give proper instructions to any professional adviser of that Party who also has an obligation to keep any such Confidential Information confidential.

1.6 The Parties shall ensure that all Confidential Information obtained from the other Party under or in connection with this PDA:-

(a) is given only to such of its employees, professional advisors or consultants engaged to advise it in connection with this PDA as is strictly necessary for the performance of this PDA and only to the extent necessary for the performance of this PDA;

(b) is treated as confidential and not disclosed (without Homes England’s prior written approval) or used by any such staff or professional advisors or consultants otherwise than for the purposes of this PDA and in all instances such third parties are subject to a signed confidentiality undertaking.

1.7 Notwithstanding any other provision of this PDA, nothing in this agreement shall prevent the Partners:

(a) disclosing any Confidential Information for the purpose of:

(i) the examination and certification of its accounts; or

(ii) any examination pursuant to section 6(1) of the National Audit Act 1983 of the economy, efficiency and effectiveness with which Homes England has used its resources; or

(b) disclosing any Confidential Information to any other department, office or agency of the Crown provided that in disclosing such Confidential Information pursuant to this paragraph (b), it discloses only the information which is necessary for the purpose concerned and requires that the information is treated in confidence;

(c) publishing the Agreement to the general public in its entirety (but with any information, which is exempt from disclosure in accordance with the provisions of the FOIA, redacted) and in the case of North East MSA disclosing the terms of the Agreement to its constituent councils and non-constituent councils.

1.8 Save as otherwise set out in this clause 1, no Party shall, and each Party shall use reasonable endeavours to ensure that no contractor, officer, employee or agent shall, communicate with any representative of any press, television, radio or other communications media on any matter concerning this PDA without the other Party’s prior written consent (in each case, not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed).

2. Freedom of information

2.1 In this clause the following words and expressions have the following meaning:

Freedom of Information Laws means the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 and any subordinate legislation made thereunder from time to time together with any guidance and/or codes of practice issued by the Information Commissioner in relation to such legislation;

2.2 The Parties are each a public authority as defined under the Freedom of Information Laws and so may be required to disclose information in response to a request for information under those laws (Request for Information). The Party in receipt of a Request for Information (Recipient) shall be responsible for determining whether any such information insofar as it relates to this Agreement should be disclosed pursuant to a Request for Information and will:

(a) where appropriate and as soon as reasonably practicable inform the other Party that it has received a request to disclose information in response to a request for information under the Freedom of Information Laws; and

(b) in relation to such information and pursuant to the Freedom of Information Laws, consider the application of the exceptions and exemptions to disclosure before complying with any obligation to disclose such information.

2.3 Nothing in this PDA will prevent any Party from complying with any valid order, decision, enforcement or practice recommendation notice issued to it by the Information Commissioner under the Freedom of Information Laws.

3. Anti bribery

3.1 The Parties shall:

(a) comply with all applicable laws, statutes, regulations, and codes relating to anti-bribery and anti-corruption including but not limited to the Bribery Act 2010 (Requirements);

(b) not engage in any activity, practice or conduct which would constitute an offence under sections 1, 2 or 6 of the Bribery Act 2010 if such activity, practice or conduct had been carried out in the UK;

(c) have and maintain in place throughout the term of this MoU its own policies and procedures, including but not limited to adequate procedures under the Bribery Act 2010, to ensure compliance with the Requirements, the Relevant Policies and paragraph (b), and will enforce them where appropriate;

3.2 The Parties shall ensure that any person who is performing services or providing goods in connection with this Agreement does so only on the basis of a written contract which imposes on and secures from such person obligations in the same terms as paragraphs (a) to (c) above and also an obligation to immediately report to the appointing party any request or demand for any undue financial or other advantage of any kind received by them in connection with the performance of such services or the provision of such goods and to (at the request of the appointing party) produce a written certificate confirming compliance with the anti-bribery requirements and to provide such supporting evidence of compliance as the appointing party may reasonably request.
